correctness.rationale: Common unitary triangularization exists by joint commutativity. The two diagonal tuples are in the domain by compression of each strict rectangular block. For distinct tuples, commutativity makes every upper-right entry a fixed scalar c times the difference of the two corresponding diagonal entries, so the holomorphic calculus on joint data has the stated two-value form. For repeated tuples the square-zero parts give the first derivative instead. The lifted automorphism identity works without entry commutativity at the block level: with W=Z−B, one can rewrite Φ_B= D_{B*}(I−ZB*)⁻¹W D_B⁻¹ using B*D_{B*}⁻²=D_B⁻²B*. Factoring the defect, the middle block is (I−ZB*)D_{B*}⁻²(I−BZ*)−W D_B⁻² W*=I−ZZ*, by expansion. This supplies strictness after amplification. In the distinct case the transformed block has norm √(1+|c|²)||U_j||, and the path through wU_j/max_j||U_j|| is a common disk reaching both tuples after inverse automorphisms. Schwarz–Pick and the determinant of the triangular defect give exactly the needed contraction; the boundary-value case is constant by the maximum-modulus principle. In the repeated case the lifted strict norm bounds the derivative direction after centering; the same radial disk yields the Schwarz–Pick jet bound |df(v)|≤1−|f(λ)|², exactly the repeated-diagonal defect condition. Constants attain one. HRS Proposition 3.5 gives a scalar polynomial witness on a row ball of dimension two; shrinking preserves a strict violation, embedding into a row or the adjoint pair into a column preserves the strict block norm, and the scalar supremum on the larger ball remains one because the selected row or column is a contraction and its embedded two-ball is contained in the full ball. Direct sums with zero coordinates also propagate the violation to all larger operator sizes.
residual_risks: The claim reviewed uses strict block norms and scalar holomorphic functions. The frozen numerical script only tests finite identities and examples. The asserted failure at size three is for individual non-disc factors, not a blanket claim about every product.

The strongest checked exact one-factor result and broader conditional estimates do not supply this conclusion.

value.rationale: The result answers a sharp contractivity question in a natural finite operator size for a whole domain class, not just a low-dimensional scalar parameter slice. Removing the bounded Gleason hypothesis for all genuine rectangular factors at size two and giving exact constant one sharpens general level estimates in a regime where the next size can already fail. The size-three counterexample is context and is not counted as a new contribution.
residual_risks: Does not give optimal bounds above size two or assert matrix-valued contractivity.
